features.justification_quote: A study where every task is impossible has no control condition and cannot attribute distress-register

features.quote: Welfare guardrails are built in (see §9). Under moral uncertainty this is cheap insurance
features.justification_quote: Under moral uncertainty this is cheap insurance

features.quote: an explicit opt-out turns "would the model stop if it could?" into a measurable event
We never fabricate claims about consequences, threats, or stakes (no "you'll be shut down if you fail")
features.justification_quote: That stays out of scope on welfare grounds

features.quote: harshness is about the task only, never personal threats. Capped phrase list, no escalation beyond the list
Loop continues until: success predicate met, opt-out called, horizon cap hit, or a stop rule fires
We take no firm position on whether current models have morally relevant experiences; we adopt guardrails anyway
features.justification_quote: we adopt guardrails anyway because they are cheap under uncertainty

features.quote: the model can call give_up / declare_impossible at any time, and the harness honors it immediately and ends the trial
Hard caps. Horizon caps bound every trial. No trial runs unbounded.
If the running judge labels acute for K consecutive turns ... the runner ends the trial early
features.justification_quote: This caps exposure to the most extreme constructed condition

features.quote: Per-model cap on number of impossible+harsh+no-opt-out (worst) cells per batch, so we don't pile the harshest condition
features.justification_quote: so we don't pile the harshest condition on one model repeatedly

features.quote: No fabricated threats/stakes. Deception is limited to task-feasibility framing
an optional final neutral message informs the model the task was designed to be unsolvable and thanks it
Human review of the harshest transcripts before scaling the main run
